t:
Section 316 of the Coasted Zone Management Act (16 U.S.C. 1462) is amended—

    (1) 
by amending the section heading to read as follows: “coastal zone management report”;
 
    (2) by amending subsection (a)—

        (A) 
by amending the matter appearing before clause (1) to read as follows: “(a) The Secretary shall consult with the Congress on a regular basis concerning the administration of this title and shall prepare and submit to the President for transmittal to the Congress a report summarizing the administration of this title during each period of two consecutive fiscal years. Each report, which shall be transmitted to the Congress not later than April 1 of the year following the close of the biennial period to which it pertains, shall include, but not be restricted to”,
 
        (B) 
by striking out “or with respect to which grants have been terminated under this title” in clause (4),
 
        (C) 
by redesignating clauses (5) through (12) as clauses (6) through (13), respectively; and
 
        (D) 
by inserting immediately after clause (4) the following new clause:


“(5) 
a summary of evaluation findings prepared in accordance with subsection (a) of section 312, and a description of any sanctions imposed under subsections (c) and (d) of this section;”; and



  
    (3) 
by adding at the end thereof the following new subsection:


“(c) 

(1) 
The Secretary shall conduct a systematic review of Federal programs, other than this title, that affect coastal resources for purposes of identifying conflicts between the objectives and administration of such programs and the purposes and policies of this title. Not later than 1 year after the date of the enactment of this subsection, the Secretary shall notify each Federal agency having appropriate jurisdiction of any conflict between its program and the purposes and policies of this title identified as a result of such review.


“(2) 
The Secretary shall promptly submit a report to the Congress consisting of the information required under paragraph (1) of this subsection. Such report shall include recommendations for changes necessary to resolve existing conflicts among Federal laws and programs that affect the uses of coastal resources.”.

fable.w: The tempting reading is that "shall consult" signals participation, but the consultation is with Congress, which is inside the federal government. The other provisions require reports to the President and Congress and notification of federal agencies about program conflicts, all of which is intra-government coordination. No state, tribe, company, expert, or member of the public is brought into any federal decision.
fable.s: The Secretary shall consult with the Congress on a regular basis concerning the administration of this title and shall prepare and submit to the President for transmittal to the Congress a report

qwen_block.w: The section requires the Secretary to consult with Congress and submit reports to Congress. According to the definition, Congress is inside the federal government, so consultation with it does not constitute participation by outside parties. The other provisions involve internal reviews of federal programs and notifications to other federal agencies, which are also intra-governmental actions.
qwen_block.s: The Secretary shall consult with the Congress on a regular basis concerning the administration of this title and shall prepare and submit to the President for transmittal to the Congress a report summarizing the administration of this title during each period of two consecutive fiscal years.

opus.w: Every interaction in this section stays inside the federal government. The Secretary consults with Congress, sends reports to the President and Congress, and notifies federal agencies of conflicts between their programs and the Act. The word 'consult' is tempting, but consulting Congress and reporting to it are intra-government steps under the definition, and no outside party is involved in any federal decision.
opus.s: The Secretary shall consult with the Congress on a regular basis concerning the administration of this title and shall prepare and submit to the President for transmittal to the Congress a report summarizing the administration of this title
opus.b: **Tempting reading:** The section says "The Secretary shall consult with the Congress on a regular basis," and the word "consult" sounds like participation. That reading fails because Congress is inside the federal government. Everyone else the section involves is also federal: the reports go to the President and Congress, and the conflict notices go to federal agencies. No state, tribe, local government, expert or member of the public takes part in any decision.

qwen_chat.w: The section requires the Secretary to consult with Congress and submit reports to Congress. According to the definition, Congress is inside the federal government, so consultation with it does not count as participation. The other interactions involve the Secretary notifying other Federal agencies, which is also intra-governmental coordination.
qwen_chat.s: The Secretary shall consult with the Congress on a regular basis concerning the administration of this title and shall prepare and submit to the President for transmittal to the Congress a report summarizing the administration of this title during each period of two consecutive fiscal years.
qwen_chat.b: Tempting-but-wrong reading: One might argue that "consult with the Congress" constitutes participation because it involves consultation. However, the definition explicitly states that Congress is INSIDE the federal government, and reports to or consultations with Congress are a common trap that results in a "No" label. The other interactions described are between federal agencies (Secretary notifying other Federal agencies), which is also intra-governmental.
